domain_entities.name: LeaveRequest
domain_entities.purpose: Represents an employee's application for leave. Tracks the full lifecycle from draft through submission, approval/rejection, and cancellation.

domain_entities.name: LeaveType
domain_entities.purpose: Enumeration of leave categories. Each type carries distinct entitlement, accrual, and approval rules governed by LeavePolicy.

domain_entities.name: LeaveBalance
domain_entities.purpose: Tracks an employee's leave entitlement, consumption, and remaining balance for a specific policy and fiscal year. Recalculated on every approved leave and on accrual events.

domain_entities.name: LeavePolicy
domain_entities.purpose: Defines the rules governing a specific leave type: how many days are entitled, how they accrue, notice requirements, and whether manager approval is needed. Policies are configured by HR admins.

domain_entities.name: Employee
domain_entities.purpose: Represents an employee in the organization. Tracks employment status, reporting hierarchy (managerId), and department. Employment status gates leave eligibility.

business_rules: LeaveRequest lifecycle transitions: DRAFT→SUBMITTED (employee submits), SUBMITTED→APPROVED (manager/HR admin approves), SUBMITTED→REJECTED (manager/HR admin rejects), DRAFT→CANCELLED (employee cancels draft), SUBMITTED→CANCELLED (employee withdraws pending request), APPROVED→CANCELLED (employee cancels previously approved leave — triggers balance restoration). [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest appears, not only here]

LeaveBalance lifecycle transitions: ACTIVE→EXHAUSTED (remainingDays reaches 0 after deduction), EXHAUSTED→ACTIVE (accrual or restoration adds days back), ACTIVE→FROZEN (employee terminated or policy inactivated), FROZEN→ACTIVE (employee reactivated and policy active). [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveBalance appears, not only here]

LeavePolicy lifecycle transitions: ACTIVE→INACTIVE (HR admin deactivates policy — existing balances under this policy become FROZEN), INACTIVE→ACTIVE (HR admin reactivates policy — balances unfreeze). [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeavePolicy appears, not only here]
startDate must be on or before endDate. A leave request with startDate after endDate is invalid. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest appears, not only here]

An employee must not have two or more LeaveRequests with overlapping date ranges in non-terminal states (DRAFT, SUBMITTED, APPROVED). Overlap check: two date ranges [A.start, A.end] and [B.start, B.end] overlap if A.start <= B.end AND B.start <= A.end. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest appears, not only here]

On APPROVED transition: the system deducts the requested number of days from the employee's LeaveBalance for the matching policy and fiscal year. Deduction must be atomic with the status change. If remainingDays < requested days, the transition is rejected with an insufficient-balance error. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest, LeaveBalance appears, not only here]

When a LeavePolicy has minimumNoticeDays set, the LeaveRequest's startDate must be at least minimumNoticeDays after the submission date (SUBMITTED transition timestamp). If the policy's minimumNoticeDays is null, no notice constraint applies. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest, LeavePolicy appears, not only here]

When a LeavePolicy has requiresManagerApproval = false, the LeaveRequest transitions directly from SUBMITTED to APPROVED without a manager review step. When requiresManagerApproval = true, only the employee's manager (Employee.managerId) or an HR admin can approve/reject. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest, LeavePolicy appears, not only here]

On APPROVED→CANCELLED transition: the previously deducted days are restored to the employee's LeaveBalance. The restoration must be atomic with the status change. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest, LeaveBalance appears, not only here]

Only the owning employee can transition DRAFT→SUBMITTED or DRAFT→CANCELLED. Only a manager (the employee's managerId) or HR admin can transition SUBMITTED→APPROVED or SUBMITTED→REJECTED. The owning employee can transition SUBMITTED→CANCELLED (withdraw). The owning employee can transition APPROVED→CANCELLED. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest appears, not only here]

A LeaveRequest in a terminal state (APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED) cannot transition to any other state except APPROVED→CANCELLED. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest appears, not only here]

An employee with employmentStatus 'TERMINATED' cannot create or submit new LeaveRequests. Existing APPROVED requests for a terminated employee remain valid (they may represent leave taken before termination). [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest, Employee appears, not only here]

remainingDays must always equal totalEntitlement - usedDays. This invariant must hold after every mutation. Any operation that would violate it is rejected. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveBalance appears, not only here]

When a LeavePolicy transitions ACTIVE→INACTIVE, all LeaveBalance records referencing that policy transition ACTIVE→FROZEN. When the policy transitions back INACTIVE→ACTIVE, all FROZEN balances for that policy transition back to ACTIVE (or EXHAUSTED if remainingDays = 0). [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveBalance, LeavePolicy appears, not only here]

Emergency leave (leaveType = 'emergency') bypasses the minimumNoticeDays check regardless of the policy's minimumNoticeDays value. The notice constraint is not enforced for emergency leave submissions. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest, LeavePolicy appears, not only here]
domain_notes:
## Lifecycle states introduced

- **LeaveRequest**: DRAFT, SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED — all five states already present in existing DOMAIN.md LeaveStatus enum. Transitions are governed by RBAC (employee owns DRAFT→SUBMITTED, DRAFT→CANCELLED, SUBMITTED→CANCELLED, APPROVED→CANCELLED; manager/HR admin owns SUBMITTED→APPROVED, SUBMITTED→REJECTED). Terminal states (APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED) are immutable except APPROVED→CANCELLED.
- **LeaveBalance**: ACTIVE, EXHAUSTED, FROZEN — new states beyond the existing generic 'status: string'. EXHAUSTED when remainingDays=0; FROZEN when the associated policy is deactivated or the employee is terminated.
- **LeavePolicy**: ACTIVE, INACTIVE — replaces the existing boolean isActive with explicit lifecycle states. Policy deactivation cascades to freeze all associated balances.
- **Employee**: ACTIVE, INACTIVE, TERMINATED — already present in existing DOMAIN.md as employmentStatus enum.

## Key business rules summary

- Date validity: startDate <= endDate (broad rule)
- No overlapping leave in non-terminal states (broad rule)
- Balance deduction on APPROVED; restoration on APPROVED→CANCELLED; both atomic
- remainingDays = totalEntitlement - usedDays invariant
- minimumNoticeDays enforced on submission except for emergency leave
- Auto-approval when requiresManagerApproval = false
- Terminated employees cannot create/submit new leave
- Policy deactivation freezes all associated balances; reactivation unfreezes them

## Open questions for chief architect

1. Day-counting semantics (calendar vs business days) — affects every deduction and overlap check
2. Fiscal year boundary definition and cross-year leave handling
3. Half-day leave support and modeling approach

open_questions.question: How are leave days counted from startDate and endDate? Is it inclusive calendar days (endDate - startDate + 1), business days only (excluding weekends/holidays), or half-day granularity? This affects deduction amounts, balance sufficiency checks, and overlap detection.
open_questions.impact: Every balance deduction, sufficiency check, and overlap calculation depends on this. Getting it wrong means incorrect balance tracking across the entire module.
candidate_options: Inclusive calendar days: days = endDate - startDate + 1
Business days only (Mon-Fri, excluding public holidays)
Configurable per LeavePolicy (e.g. a 'countsWeekends' boolean on the policy)

open_questions.question: What defines the fiscal year boundary for LeaveBalance? When a leave request spans two fiscal years, does it draw from one balance or split across two?
open_questions.impact: Determines which LeaveBalance record(s) are affected by a deduction. A cross-year leave request could require splitting the deduction across two balances, or the system could reject cross-year requests.
candidate_options: Custom fiscal year start month configured globally (e.g. April–March)

open_questions.question: Is half-day leave supported? If so, how is it modeled — a boolean flag, or time components on startDate/endDate?
open_questions.impact: Affects the day-counting formula, balance deduction amounts (0.5 vs 1.0), and overlap detection logic.
candidate_options: Half-day leave is not supported — minimum unit is 1 full day
Half-day leave is supported via a boolean flag on LeaveRequest (isHalfDay: boolean)
Half-day leave is supported via time-of-day on startDate/endDate
